Risk ratios

Author

Alexander W. Gofton & Emily Smith

Published

March 13, 2026

Setup

Load packages for epidemiological risk ratio calculations, model tidying, data manipulation, and plot composition.

library(epitools)
library(broom)
library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)

Plot Theme

Configure the global ggplot theme for risk ratio forest plots.

theme_set(
  theme_classic() +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(size = 11, angle = 45, hjust = 1),
      axis.title.x = element_text(size = 12),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 11),
      axis.title.y = element_text(size = 12),
      axis.line = element_line(colour = "grey70"),
      axis.ticks = element_line(colour = "grey70"),
      text = element_text(family = "Arial"),
      panel.grid.major.x = element_line(linewidth = 0.1, colour = "grey70"),
      panel.grid.minor.x = element_line(linewidth = 0.05, colour = "grey70")
    )
)

Load Data

Import the preprocessed datasets with age categories for both deduplicated and full (with repeat tests) datasets.

data_no_multi <- read_csv("data/preprocessed_no_multi_with_age_cat.csv")
data_with_multi <- read_csv("data/preprocessed_with_multi_with_age_cat.csv")

Cross-Tabulation: Age by Sex

Create a summary table of positive and negative test counts by age category and sex, with derived metrics including male-to-female ratios and positivity percentages.

age_by_sex_data <- data_no_multi %>%
  count(Age_cat, Sex, Status) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = c(Status, Sex), values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
  mutate(
    Total = Negative_F + Positive_F + Negative_M + Positive_M,
    Total_F = Negative_F + Positive_F,
    Total_M = Negative_M + Positive_M, # Fixed: was Negative_M + Negative_M
    MF_ratio = Total_M / Total_F,
    Positive = Positive_F + Positive_M,
    Positive_pct = (Positive / Total) * 100,
    Positive_F_pct = (Positive_F / (Positive_F + Negative_F)) * 100,
    Positive_M_pct = (Positive_M / (Positive_M + Negative_M)) * 100
  )

write_csv(age_by_sex_data, "results/age_by_sex_data.csv")

Age by Sex (All Tests)

Repeat the age-sex cross-tabulation using the full dataset including repeat tests.

# age_by_sex for number of tests (with multi)
age_by_sex_data_multi <- data_with_multi %>%
  count(Age_cat, Sex, Status) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = c(Status, Sex), values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
  mutate(
    Total = Negative_F + Positive_F + Negative_M + Positive_M,
    Total_F = Negative_F + Positive_F,
    Total_M = Negative_M + Positive_M, # Fixed: was Negative_M + Negative_M
    MF_ratio = Total_M / Total_F,
    Positive = Positive_F + Positive_M,
    Positive_pct = (Positive / Total) * 100,
    Positive_F_pct = (Positive_F / (Positive_F + Negative_F)) * 100,
    Positive_M_pct = (Positive_M / (Positive_M + Negative_M)) * 100
  )

write_csv(age_by_sex_data_multi, "results/age_by_sex_with_multi_data.csv")

Risk Ratio: Females vs Males (Overall)

Calculate the overall risk ratio comparing alpha-gal positivity between females and males across all age groups using a 2x2 contingency table and Fisher’s exact test.

# Calculate overall RR for females vs males (whole dataset)
overall_sex_summary <- data_no_multi |>
  count(Sex, Status) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = Status, values_from = n, values_fill = 0)

# Extract counts
pos_M <- overall_sex_summary$Positive[overall_sex_summary$Sex == "M"]
neg_M <- overall_sex_summary$Negative[overall_sex_summary$Sex == "M"]
pos_F <- overall_sex_summary$Positive[overall_sex_summary$Sex == "F"]
neg_F <- overall_sex_summary$Negative[overall_sex_summary$Sex == "F"]

# Create 2x2 matrix: rows = sex, cols = positive/negative
overall_rr_mat <- matrix(
  c(pos_M, neg_M, pos_F, neg_F),
  nrow = 2,
  byrow = TRUE,
  dimnames = list(
    Sex = c("Male", "Female"),
    Status = c("Positive", "Negative")
  )
)

# Corrected overall sex RR with columns reversed
overall_sex_rr <- riskratio(overall_rr_mat, rev = "columns")

# Extract Row 2 (Female compared to Male)
overall_rr_results <- tibble(
  Comparison = "Female vs Male",
  RR = overall_sex_rr$measure[2, "estimate"],
  Lower_CI = overall_sex_rr$measure[2, "lower"],
  Upper_CI = overall_sex_rr$measure[2, "upper"],
  P_value = overall_sex_rr$p.value[2, "fisher.exact"]
)

print(overall_rr_results)

# If you want Male vs Female instead, calculate reciprocal
overall_rr_results_male <- tibble(
  Comparison = "Male vs Female",
  RR = 1 / overall_sex_rr$measure[2, "estimate"],
  Lower_CI = 1 / overall_sex_rr$measure[2, "upper"],  # Note: swap upper/lower
  Upper_CI = 1 / overall_sex_rr$measure[2, "lower"],
  P_value = overall_sex_rr$p.value[2, "fisher.exact"]
)

print(overall_rr_results_male)

Risk Ratio: Females vs Males by Age Category

Calculate age-stratified risk ratios comparing positivity between females and males within each 10-year age group.

calc_rr <- function(df, age_cat) {
  rr_df <- df |>
    filter(Age_cat == age_cat)

  posM <- rr_df$Positive_M
  negM <- rr_df$Total_M - rr_df$Positive_M
  posF <- rr_df$Positive_F
  negF <- rr_df$Total_F - rr_df$Positive_F

  # Correct 2x2 matrix structure
  # Rows = exposure (sex), Columns = outcome (positive, negative)
  rr_mat <- matrix(
    c(posM, negM, posF, negF),
    nrow = 2,
    byrow = TRUE,
    dimnames = list(
      Sex = c("Male", "Female"),
      Status = c("Positive", "Negative")
    )
  )

  rr <- riskratio(rr_mat)

  tibble(
    Age_cat = age_cat,
    RR = rr$measure[2, "estimate"],
    Lower_CI = rr$measure[2, "lower"],
    Upper_CI = rr$measure[2, "upper"],
    P_value = rr$p.value[2, "fisher.exact"]
  )
}
rr_0 <- calc_rr(age_by_sex_data, "0-14") #%>% mutate(Age_cat = "0-14")
rr_15 <- calc_rr(age_by_sex_data, "15-24") #%>% mutate(Age_cat = "15-24")
rr_25 <- calc_rr(age_by_sex_data, "25-34") #%>% mutate(Age_cat = "25-34")
rr_35 <- calc_rr(age_by_sex_data, "35-44") #%>% mutate(Age_cat = "35-44")
rr_45 <- calc_rr(age_by_sex_data, "45-54") #%>% mutate(Age_cat = "45-54")
rr_55 <- calc_rr(age_by_sex_data, "55-64") #%>% mutate(Age_cat = "55-64")
rr_65 <- calc_rr(age_by_sex_data, "65-74") #%>% mutate(Age_cat = "65-74")
rr_75 <- calc_rr(age_by_sex_data, "75-84") #%>% mutate(Age_cat = "75-84")
rr_85 <- calc_rr(age_by_sex_data, "85+") #%>% mutate(Age_cat = "85+")

rr_sex_by_age <- bind_rows(
  rr_0,
  rr_15,
  rr_25,
  rr_35,
  rr_45,
  rr_55,
  rr_65,
  rr_75,
  rr_85
)
# results
print(rr_sex_by_age)

write.csv(rr_sex_by_age, "results/rr_sex_by_age.csv", row.names = FALSE)

Forest Plot: Sex-Stratified Risk Ratios

Create a horizontal forest plot showing female-vs-male risk ratios by age category with 95% confidence intervals.

desired_order <-
  c(
    "0-14",
    "15-24",
    "25-34",
    "35-44",
    "45-54",
    "55-64",
    "65-74",
    "75-84",
    "85+"
  )

rr_sex_by_age$Age_cat <- factor(rr_sex_by_age$Age_cat, levels = desired_order)

rr_sex_by_age_plot <- rr_sex_by_age %>%
  mutate(
    significant = ifelse(P_value < 0.05, "Significant", "Not Significant")
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Age_cat, y = RR)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "red", size = 0.8) +
  geom_point(aes(shape = significant), color = "black", size = 4) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(ymin = Lower_CI, ymax = Upper_CI),
    color = "black",
    width = 0.3,
    linewidth = 0.8
  ) +
  scale_shape_manual(
    values = c("Significant" = 16, "Not Significant" = 1),
    guide = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 3))
  ) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_x_discrete(
    labels = c(
      "0-14" = "0-14",
      "15-24" = "15-24",
      "25-34" = "25-34",
      "35-44" = "35-44",
      "45-54" = "45-54",
      "55-64" = "55-64",
      "65-74" = "65-74",
      "75-84" = "75-84",
      "85+" = "85+"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    #title = "Female Risk Ratios by Age Group",
    #subtitle = "Reference: Males in same age group.",
    y = "Risk Ratio",
    x = "Age Category",
    shape = "Statistical Significance"
  ) +
  guides(
    shape = guide_legend(override.aes = list(color = "black"))
  ) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank()
  )

rr_sex_by_age_plot
# Save plot
ggsave(
  "plots/risk_ratio_sex_by_age.png",
  rr_sex_by_age_plot,
  width = 12,
  height = 12,
  units = "cm",
  bg = "transparent"
)

Risk Ratios for Age-Sex Combinations

Calculate risk ratios for each age-sex group relative to females aged 25-34 as the reference population, with Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons.

calc_combined_rr <- function(
  data,
  age_cat,
  sex,
  ref_age = "25-34",
  ref_sex = "F"
) {
  # Target group
  target_data <- data |>
    filter(Age_cat == age_cat, Sex == sex) |>
    count(Status) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = Status, values_from = n, values_fill = 0)

  # Reference group
  ref_data <- data |>
    filter(Age_cat == ref_age, Sex == ref_sex) |>
    count(Status) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = Status, values_from = n, values_fill = 0)

  # Correct matrix: rows = groups, cols = positive/negative
  rr_mat <- matrix(
    c(
      target_data$Positive,
      target_data$Negative,
      ref_data$Positive,
      ref_data$Negative
    ),
    nrow = 2,
    byrow = TRUE
  )

  rr_result <- riskratio(rr_mat, rev = "columns")

  tibble(
    Age_cat = age_cat,
    Sex = sex,
    RR = rr_result$measure[2, "estimate"],
    Lower_CI = rr_result$measure[2, "lower"],
    Upper_CI = rr_result$measure[2, "upper"],
    P_value = rr_result$p.value[2, "fisher.exact"]
  )
}
# Calculate combined risk ratios using Male 25-34 as reference
age_sex_combinations <- expand_grid(
  Age_cat = unique(data_no_multi$Age_cat),
  Sex = c("M", "F")
) %>%
  filter(!(Age_cat == "25-34" & Sex == "F")) # Remove reference group

combined_rr_results <- map2_dfr(
  age_sex_combinations$Age_cat,
  age_sex_combinations$Sex,
  ~ calc_combined_rr(data_no_multi, .x, .y)
) |>
  mutate(
    # Bonferroni correction for 17 comparisons
    P_value_adj = p.adjust(P_value, method = "bonferroni"),
    significant_raw = P_value < 0.05,
    significant_adj = P_value_adj < 0.05
  )

print("Risk ratios using Females 25-34 as reference:")
print(combined_rr_results)

write.csv(
  combined_rr_results,
  "results/combined_rr_results.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

Forest Plot: Combined Age-Sex Risk Ratios

Create a forest plot showing risk ratios for all age-sex combinations relative to the reference group, colour-coded by sex and with significance indicators.

MALE_COLOR <- "#0072B2"
FEMALE_COLOR <- "#D55E00"

plot_data <- combined_rr_results %>%
  mutate(
    # Create a combined label for better visualization
    group_label = paste0(Age_cat, " ", Sex),
    # Create significance indicator
    significant = ifelse(P_value < 0.05, "Significant", "Not Significant"),
    # Create proper ordering: first by age, then by sex within age
    Age_cat = factor(
      Age_cat,
      levels = c(
        "0-14",
        "15-24",
        "25-34",
        "35-44",
        "45-54",
        "55-64",
        "65-74",
        "75-84",
        "85+"
      )
    ),
    Sex = factor(Sex, levels = c("M", "F")),
    # Create ordered factor for y-axis that respects age then sex ordering
    group_label = factor(
      group_label,
      levels = expand_grid(
        Age_cat = c(
          "0-14",
          "15-24",
          "25-34",
          "35-44",
          "45-54",
          "55-64",
          "65-74",
          "75-84",
          "85+"
        ),
        Sex = c("M", "F")
      ) %>%
        filter(!(Age_cat == "25-34" & Sex == "F")) %>% # Remove reference
        mutate(label = paste(Age_cat, Sex)) %>%
        pull(label)
    )
  )
plot_data <- plot_data %>%
  mutate(
    Sex_label = case_when(
      Sex == "M" ~ "Male",
      Sex == "F" ~ "Female"
    )
  )

combined_rr_results_plot <- plot_data %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = RR, y = group_label)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "red", size = 1) +
  geom_point(aes(color = Sex_label, shape = significant), size = 4) +
  geom_errorbarh(
    aes(xmin = Lower_CI, xmax = Upper_CI, color = Sex_label),
    height = 0.3,
    linewidth = 0.8
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    name = "Sex",
    values = c("Male" = MALE_COLOR, "Female" = FEMALE_COLOR)
  ) +
  scale_shape_manual(
    name = "Statistical Significance",
    values = c("Significant" = 16, "Not Significant" = 1),
    guide = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 3))
  ) +
  labs(
    #title = "Risk Ratios for Age-Sex Combinations",
    #subtitle = "Reference: Male 25-34 years",
    x = "Risk Ratio (RR)",
    y = "Age-Sex Category"
  ) +
  guides(
    color = guide_legend(
      override.aes = list(shape = 16),
      order = 1
    ),
    shape = guide_legend(
      override.aes = list(color = "black"),
      order = 2
    )
  ) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.box = "vertical",
    legend.spacing = unit(0.5, "cm"),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(size = 0.1, colour = "grey70")
  )

# Extract the plot and legends
combined_rr_results_plot_final <- combined_rr_results_plot +
  theme(
    axis.title.y = element_text(hjust = 0.5, margin = margin(r = 8)),

Risk Ratios by Age Group

Calculate risk ratios comparing positivity in each age group to the 25-34 reference group, pooling both sexes.

# Create age data
age_data <- age_by_sex_data %>%
  dplyr::select(Age_cat, Total, Positive, Positive_pct)
calc_rr_age_vs_ref <- function(df, age_cat, ref_cat = "25-34") {
  # Get row for target age group
  group_df <- df %>% filter(Age_cat == age_cat)
  pos_group <- group_df$Positive
  neg_group <- group_df$Total - pos_group

  # Get row for reference age group
  ref_df <- df %>% filter(Age_cat == ref_cat)
  pos_ref <- ref_df$Positive
  neg_ref <- ref_df$Total - pos_ref

  # Construct 2x2 matrix: rows = group, ref; cols = positive, negative
  rr_mat <- matrix(
    c(pos_group, neg_group, pos_ref, neg_ref),
    nrow = 2,
    byrow = TRUE,
    dimnames = list(
      Group = c(age_cat, ref_cat),
      Status = c("Positive", "Negative")
    )
  )

  # Calculate risk ratio
  rr <- suppressWarnings(riskratio(rr_mat, rev = "columns"))

  # Extract RR for comparison row
  tibble(
    Age_cat = age_cat,
    RR = rr$measure[2, "estimate"],
    Lower_CI = rr$measure[2, "lower"],
    Upper_CI = rr$measure[2, "upper"],
    P_value = rr$p.value[2, "fisher.exact"]
  )
}
# Calculate for each age group vs 25-34
rr_age <- bind_rows(
  calc_rr_age_vs_ref(age_data, "0-14"),
  calc_rr_age_vs_ref(age_data, "15-24"),
  calc_rr_age_vs_ref(age_data, "45-54"),
  calc_rr_age_vs_ref(age_data, "55-64"),
  calc_rr_age_vs_ref(age_data, "65-74"),
  calc_rr_age_vs_ref(age_data, "75-84"),
  calc_rr_age_vs_ref(age_data, "85+")
)

print(rr_age)

Forest Plot: Age-Stratified Risk Ratios

Create a horizontal forest plot showing age-group risk ratios with 95% confidence intervals and significance markers.

# Plot
rr_age_plot <- rr_age %>%
  mutate(
    significant = ifelse(P_value < 0.05, "Significant", "Not Significant")
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Age_cat, y = RR)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "red", size = 0.8) +
  geom_point(aes(shape = significant), color = "black", size = 4) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(ymin = Lower_CI, ymax = Upper_CI),
    color = "black",
    width = 0.3,
    linewidth = 0.8
  ) +
  scale_shape_manual(
    values = c("Significant" = 16, "Not Significant" = 1),
    guide = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 3))
  ) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    #title = "Risk Ratios of Positivity by Age Group",
    #subtitle = "Reference: 25-34 age group.",
    y = "Risk Ratio",
    x = "Age Category",
    shape = "Statistical Significance"
  ) +
  guides(
    shape = guide_legend(override.aes = list(color = "black"))
  ) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank()
  )

rr_age_plot

  rr_age_plot,
  width = 12,
  height = 12,
  units = "cm",

)

Mantel-Haenszel Test

Perform the Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test for conditional independence to assess whether the sex-positivity association is consistent across age strata.

# Create stratified analysis - convert to 3D array
mh_data <- data_no_multi %>%
  count(Age_cat, Sex, Status) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Status, values_from = n, values_fill = 0)

# Create a 3D array: [Sex, Status, Age_cat]
# Dimensions: 2 (M/F) x 2 (Positive/Negative) x 8 (age groups)
mh_array <- array(
  dim = c(2, 2, length(unique(mh_data$Age_cat))),
  dimnames = list(
    Sex = c("F", "M"),
    Status = c("Positive", "Negative"),
    Age_cat = sort(unique(mh_data$Age_cat))
  )
)

# Fill the array
for (i in seq_along(unique(mh_data$Age_cat))) {
  age_group <- sort(unique(mh_data$Age_cat))[i]
  age_data <- mh_data %>% filter(Age_cat == age_group)

  # Female counts
  mh_array["F", "Positive", i] <- age_data$Positive[age_data$Sex == "F"]
  mh_array["F", "Negative", i] <- age_data$Negative[age_data$Sex == "F"]

  # Male counts
  mh_array["M", "Positive", i] <- age_data$Positive[age_data$Sex == "M"]
  mh_array["M", "Negative", i] <- age_data$Negative[age_data$Sex == "M"]
}

# Perform Mantel-Haenszel test
mh_result <- mantelhaen.test(mh_array)
print(mh_result)
